subject.title: [Feature]: When messages are merged and processed, the agent event is expected to carry the original runId(s)

question: Should merged queued Gateway events preserve the executed runId and add an original/source run ID array, or should merged execution reuse one of the source run IDs as the public runId?
rationale: Current code tracks queued identities internally, but this issue changes a stable public Gateway event contract and proposes competing API semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Add additive lineage array
options.body: Preserve the executed runId and add a named array such as originalRunIds or sourceRunIds to public event schemas and projections.

options.title: Reuse one source ID
options.body: Make merged execution appear under the first or last queued source ID, which may help simple clients but hides multi-source lineage and changes run identity semantics.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave clients to correlate through accepted/final events and session history, accepting that merged queued execution cannot be mapped one-to-one from live agent events.

recommendation.title: Add additive lineage array
recommendation.body: Preserve the executed runId and add a named array such as originalRunIds or sourceRunIds to public event schemas and projections.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision is a public Gateway protocol/API contract question, and steipete has the strongest protocol and Gateway feature-history signal among the likely owners.
